title: Crime and Intelligence Analysis
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: CRIME AND INTELLIGENCE ANALYSIS Certificate of Achievement (STATE CODE 43713)
outcomes: Developing Analytical Skills: The primary objective is to help students develop strong analytical skills, enabling them to examine complex data, identify patterns and draw meaningful conclusions. This involves learning about various analytical techniques and tools commonly used in crime and intelligence analysis.

Understanding Criminal Behavior: Students will learn the fundamentals of criminal behavior, including criminological theories, modus operandi, and the psychology behind criminal activities. Understanding why criminals act the way they do is crucial for effective analysis.

Data Collection and Management: Participants will learn how to gather, organize, and manage data related to criminal activities and intelligence sources. This includes using databases, data mining techniques, and ensuring data security and confidentiality.

Crime Pattern Recognition: One of the key objectives is to train individuals in recognizing crime patterns and trends. Identifying recurring patterns can assist public and private sector agencies in predicting and preventing future criminal incidents.
Intelligence Gathering and Analysis: Students will learn how to collect intelligence from various sources, such as surveillance, informants, and open-source data.

Ethical and Legal Considerations: Students will learn about the ethical and legal considerations involved in crime and intelligence analysis ensuring that all activities are carried out responsibly and within the bounds of the law.

Preparation for Employment: The Crime and Intelligence Analysis Certificate aims to prepare students for non-sworn careers in law enforcement on a local, state, and federal level, intelligence agencies in both the public and private sector, and private security firms.
